articles.title: GHSA: @hono/node-server: Backslash in the request path is parsed as a path separator, bypassing path-based access control at a reverse proxy
articles.summary:
### Summary

`@hono/node-server` passes the raw request-target to the WHATWG URL parser, which treats a backslash in the path as `/` and then resolves `..` segments. A request for `/admin\secret` or `/public\..\admin/secret` reaches the application as `/admin/secret`. articles.title: GHSA: Loofah: SVG `<textPath>` and `<mpath>` bypass local-reference restriction
articles.summary:
## Summary

Loofah restricts `href` and `xlink:href` on certain SVG elements to same-document references. Two elements escaped the restriction:

- `<textPath>`: `SVG_ALLOW_LOCAL_HREF` listed it in lowercase as `textpath`, but the HTML5 parser names the element `textPath` inside `<svg>`, so the check never matched on the HTML5 path.

articles.title: USN-9068-1: Debian-LAN vulnerability
articles.summary: Wolfgang Schweer discovered that Debian-LAN configured overly permissive ACLs for the Kerberos admin server. An authenticated user could possibly use this issue to change the credentials of other users, leading to privilege escalation.

articles.title: GHSA: Loofah: Regular expression denial of service in the SVG local-reference check
articles.summary:
## Summary

Loofah's HTML5 sanitizer restricts the `href` and `xlink:href` attributes of SVG reference elements to local references. That check matched the attribute value against `/^\s*[^#\s].*/m`. In Ruby `^` anchors to every line start and `\s` matches newlines, so an all-whitespace value made the engine rescan the value from each of its line starts, taking time quadratic in its length.

articles.title: USN-9085-1: Ruby OpenID vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that Ruby OpenID sent a request to the claimed identifier URL before verifying the signature of an OpenID response. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to perform server-side request forgery attacks.

articles.title: USN-9084-1: Radicale vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that Radicale did not delay failed authentication attempts when using htpasswd authentication. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain user passwords through timing or brute-force attacks.

articles.title: GHSA: Loofah: Mutation XSS in the HTML5 scrubbers through unescaped attribute values
articles.summary:
## Summary

Loofah's HTML5 scrubbers could emit output that a browser parses into different markup, allowing mutation XSS. Nokogiri < 1.19.5 did not escape `<` and `>` in attribute values. When the output contained certain MathML, a browser treated markup inside an allowed attribute as live HTML. The `:strip` scrubber is affected in every browser. articles.summary:

### Patches
